data.title: Collected Data Staged and Archived
data.summary: Before exfiltration, the sample consolidates everything it has gathered — captured input, documents, screenshots — into a single compressed or encrypted archive, usually via a bundled or living-off-the-land utility.
data.description:
Staging reduces exfiltration to a single transfer rather than many small ones, which is
both more efficient for the operator and less noisy against egress monitoring tuned to spot
repeated small connections. The archiving step itself — a call to a bundled compression
library, or shelling out to a system utility like tar or a scripting host's native
compression — is often a useful detection point, since it is a distinct, loggable event
separate from the collection that preceded it.
data.recommendation:
* Hunt for archive creation events (file-creation of .zip/.rar/.7z/.tar in unusual locations, or command-line invocation of archive utilities) as a staging signal independent of the collection techniques feeding it.
* Recover the staged archive if it has not yet been exfiltrated — it is a direct inventory of everything collected, with no inference needed.
* Correlate archive creation timing against collection events to establish the collection window precisely.
data.short_recommendation: Hunt for archive-creation events as a staging signal distinct from the collection techniques feeding it.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Invoked a bundled compression routine to bundle captured files into a single encrypted archive prior to upload.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Consolidated captured files into a password-protected archive using a statically linked compression library.
